publisher: Landesamt für Einwanderung (LEA) Berlin, via ServicePortal Berlin (berlin.de)
raw_extract:
Secured livelihood

Sufficient funds to secure your livelihood, including adequate health insurance coverage, are required. Sufficient funds are available if they correspond to the maximum BAföG funding rate.
For a stay for study purposes, a monthly amount of 992.00 euros must be available, i.e. 11,904.00 euros per year (current value for the year 2026).

[...]

Proof of livelihood

For the initial issue: e.g. blocked account (Sperrkonto) at a German Bank / submission of a declaration of commitment by a third party on an official form / scholarship / notarized declaration from parents securing the livelihood for the duration of the studies with proof of the income of the parents in the last six months / employment contract for a part-time job
For the extension: bank statements of the last six months, proof of other income

Legal basis: Aufenthaltsgesetz (AufenthG) § 16b
research_notes: CONFIRMED from the immigration authority itself (Landesamt für Einwanderung Berlin), not a university page or an aggregator. Financial proof for a German student residence permit (studentenrechtlicher Aufenthaltstitel) requires EUR 992.00 per month, i.e. EUR 11,904.00 per year, stated on the page as the 'current value for the year 2026'. as_of = 2026. IMPORTANT NUANCE the corpus must not flatten: the LEA names the blocked account (Sperrkonto) only as ONE of several acceptable routes ('e.g. blocked account ... / declaration of commitment by a third party / scholarship / notarized declaration from parents ... / employment contract for a part-time job'). So 'Germany requires a blocked account' is an over-statement — Germany requires PROOF OF SECURED LIVELIHOOD, of which a Sperrkonto is the most common instrument. There is no national statutory 'blocked account amount' per se: this figure is the Landesamt's statement of the maximum BAföG rate as the sufficiency benchmark, and it is reproduced by the state authority. LIMITATION/GAP: I did not reach the Federal Foreign Office's own blocked-account page, which is the federal-level source referenced by the LEA page (linked as 'Information on blocked accounts (Federal Foreign Office)'); the fee page therefore evidences the Berlin LEA's benchmark amount and its equivalence to the BAföG maximum rate. Also note the Berlin LEA issues both sticker-label and electronic (eAT) residence permits at different fees; this corpus tracks study financial proof, so permit fees are not a target metric here.
